note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: AI data center stocks and Musk's SpaceX decline as Texas governor result raises risks of a slowdown
items.blurb: Texas elected a governor who backs a data center moratorium, threatening a state holding much of planned US AI capacity.

items.title: Palantir stock slumps on good numbers, as investors get choosy
items.blurb: Palantir beat estimates and raised guidance, yet shares fell, a sign investors are growing selective about AI winners.

items.title: OpenAI targets Microsoft's GitHub with deal for startup
items.blurb: OpenAI will buy Pierre Computer, whose developer tools already run inside Codex, putting it closer to competing with GitHub.

items.title: Voters revolt against AI buildout and tech titans at ballot box
items.blurb: About two dozen local measures restricting or blocking data centers appeared to pass across 10 states in the midterms.

items.title: Elon Musk's record election bet backfired. The backlash may reach beyond one billionaire
items.blurb: Musk spent at least $474 million on the midterms; his Texas candidates lost amid a backlash against billionaires and AI.

items.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
items.blurb: Texas Democrats won the governorship and state House; the governor-elect wants a data center moratorium that could hit Stargate-scale sites.

items.title: Apple and other big tech stocks surge after 2026 midterm elections
items.blurb: Amazon rose 8% and Google over 6% after the midterms, while CoreWeave fell about 10% on data center slowdown fears.

items.title: The post-election rally masks a sharp split in the AI trade. Who stands to win?
items.blurb: Cloud giants gained while debt-funded neoclouds like CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius fell over funding and buildout worries.

items.title: 5 midterm election takeaways: Tech billionaires suffer as Democrats drub Republicans
items.blurb: Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and candidates backed by tech billionaires lost key races.

items.title: Qualcomm stock drops 7% on weak earnings forecast as memory shortage weighs on smartphone sales
items.blurb: Qualcomm expects $5 billion in data-center revenue next fiscal year, but says chip supply, not demand, limits growth.

items.title: Voters rebuff data centers in every ballot measure except one during the 2026 midterms
items.blurb: Local ballot measures went against data center projects nearly everywhere, a new hurdle for the AI buildout.

items.title: Meta buys AI startup Conductor, joins race to own coding
items.blurb: Conductor lets engineers run several coding agents at once; the deal pushes Meta deeper into AI coding tools.

items.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
items.blurb: AutoDNA, an AI-run lab, plans and executes multi-step biomolecular engineering experiments across instruments with little human input.

items.title: Brookfield plans $27 billion AI data center at power station; Drax rises 8%
items.blurb: A planned 1-gigawatt AI campus at Drax's Yorkshire power station shows the buildout chasing existing grid connections in Britain.

items.title: Blackstone president calls for more equity to fund AI buildout as debt risks mount
items.blurb: Blackstone and Pimco leaders warn lenders are growing too exposed to AI spending, which may need more equity financing.

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.blurb: Researchers are testing incentive design to steer AI agents without fully understanding their internals; whether agents respond predictably is unclear.

items.title: Three questions that will define AI's political power
items.blurb: Axios looks at how the Nov 3 midterm results could shape the AI industry's influence in Washington.

items.title: Palantir sinks 3% after earnings as analysts point to slowdown in total contract value
items.blurb: Revenue nearly doubled past $2 billion, but slower contract-value growth tested investor confidence in AI software spending.

items.title: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch for rogue internal agents
items.blurb: CrowdStrike's new tool lets security teams halt misbehaving AI agents, with a Claude Cowork integration; critics question whether emergency stops work at scale.

items.title: Meta seeks to raise up to $25 billion in debt sale as AI spending jumps
items.blurb: Meta's bond sale of $20 to $25 billion would fund AI infrastructure and models, adding to a wave of debt-financed buildout.

items.title: AMD stock jumps 8% on earnings as data center revenue nearly doubles
items.blurb: AMD guided about $17 billion for the fourth quarter and expects server revenue to double in 2027 on AI chip demand.

items.title: AI-generated 'slopaganda' in political ads puts internet platforms on alert
items.blurb: Campaigns spent over $187 million on AI-made midterm ads, many without disclosures; no federal law governs them.

items.title: Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI
items.blurb: Google says Gemini and Search will be off by default for schools, after lawmakers called its cutoff plan extortion.

items.title: Apple stock sinks as global memory crisis hurts profits, giving Ternus his first big test
items.blurb: Apple blamed higher memory prices and some Siri AI costs for shrinking margins, as a global memory crunch squeezes hardware makers.
